Executive Summary

Comparison Analysis: This report compares 5 soil samples based on grain size distribution and hydraulic conductivity estimates.

Key Findings:

  • Highest permeability: Sample_1_Odong (9.54e-04 m/s)
  • Lowest permeability: Example_2_Case_1_Vukovic_15C (1.14e-06 m/s)
  • Permeability range: 837.4x difference

Methodology

Comparative Analysis Approach

This comparison report presents a side-by-side analysis of multiple soil samples to identify patterns, variations, and relationships between grain size characteristics and hydraulic conductivity estimates.

Analysis Components

Grain Size Comparison: Overlapping distribution curves allow visual assessment of particle size variations between samples.

K-Value Comparison: Box plots and statistical summaries reveal the range and reliability of hydraulic conductivity estimates across samples.

Method Reliability: A reliability matrix shows which empirical methods are applicable for each sample, helping identify the most suitable estimation approaches.

Interpretation & Discussion

Comparative Analysis

Permeability Characteristics:

  • The highest permeability sample is Sample_1_Odong with K = 9.54e-04 m/s, classified as High (Clean Sand).
  • The lowest permeability sample is Example_2_Case_1_Vukovic_15C with K = 1.14e-06 m/s, classified as Low (Silt).
  • The 837.4-fold difference in permeability reflects the variability in grain size distribution among the samples.

Statistical Overview:

  • Average sample K geometric mean: 3.10e-04 m/s
  • Standard deviation: 3.41e-04 m/s
  • Coefficient of variation: 109.8%
